items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: When Stravinsky put the African rhythms back in to European music with Le Sacre du printemps in 1921 I think it was, it caused two days of rioting in Paris you know.

ctx.x: Yeah. It was the ballads or the European music is simply music with the rhythm removed. When Stravinsky put the African rhythms back in to European music with Le Sacre du printemps in 1921 I think it was, it caused two days of rioting in Paris you know.
Yeah. They didn’t know what to do with that.

items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Stravinsky, yeah. Because that was his favorite composer.

ctx.x: Stravinsky, yeah. Because that was his favorite composer. He was an intellectual, much more than a smoker of reefer or a shoot-up jazz musician, very much more depth to him than that. And this is the part of him that I want to cover. This was a very great man. Far greater than anybody realizes. And you only have to listen to one of his solos to hear the mental agility that inspired Coltrane and everybody else. Brilliant cat.
Amazing. You’ve got some great news regarding your vocalese school?
